segments.text: Welcome back.
Day eight, and the start of your second week.
Something may be shifting by now.
The cravings tend to come a little less often.
And in their place, you might be noticing something quieter and stranger.
Empty minutes.
The end of a meal.
Waiting for someone.
The pause between one job and the next.
Moments that used to have a shape, and now just sit there.
The night before Day Xero, I asked you a question.
Is it the nicotine you'd miss, or the five minutes?
This week you find out.
Because for years, nicotine marked your breaks for you.
It gave you a reason to step outside, and a clear end when the cigarette was finished.
The autopilot you mapped in the prep week is still looking for its cue in those moments.
And an empty minute with nothing in it is exactly where a craving finds room.
But here's the thing.
The five minutes were always yours.
Stepping away, breathing, letting your mind wander.
You were allowed those all along.
Nicotine just came along for the ride, and took the credit.
So let's take a break right now.
A real one, with nothing in it.
Look away from the screen, if you can.
Let your eyes rest on something further off.
Take a breath, in a way that feels comfortable for you.
Feel your feet on the floor.
Your shoulders.
Your hands, with nothing in them.
Notice if there's a pull to fill this.
To reach for something, check something, do something.
You don't have to answer it.
Let the minute be empty.
This is what a break feels like without the gap in it.
It may feel a little bare at first.
That passes.
An empty minute is easier when you've already decided what goes in it.
Not a rule.
A short menu.
Step outside.
Make a proper cup of something.
Stretch.
Text someone.
Look out of a window and do nothing at all.
In a moment, you'll pick three.
They'll be waiting for you in Craving SOS, so when boredom turns up, the next step is already there.
Keep the break.
It was always the good part.
I'll see you in a couple of days.
